entries.name: Ordering
entries.summary: The result of `Comparable.compare`. Declared here rather than only inside the interpreter so that `Ordering`, `Less`, `Equal` and `Greater` reach the semantic layer the same way every other stdlib type does — through the collected interfaces — instead of existing solely as native environment bindings the type checker and name resolver cannot see.

entries.name: compare
entries.summary: A total order: `compare` answers Less, Equal or Greater. `==` stays independent — a type may be Equatable without being ordered.

entries.name: Number
entries.summary: Number carries the implementation, so Integer and Float both inherit it rather than repeating the same three comparisons. Mixed receivers work because `<` and `>` promote across the two (`1.compare(1.0)` is Equal).

entries.name: identity
entries.summary: `combine` must be associative and `identity` neutral on both sides.

entries.name: repeat
entries.summary: Combines this value with itself `n` times. Repeating zero times returns the monoid identity; a negative repetition count is invalid.

entries.name: identity
entries.summary: Combining a value with its inverse must produce `identity`.

entries.name: Ordering
entries.summary:
Ordering is a Monoid under "first decision wins", with Equal as identity. That is what makes multi-key comparison compose instead of nesting ifs:

```kex
a.name.compare(b.name).combine(a.age.compare(b.age))
```

`combine` evaluates its argument eagerly, so the later comparison runs even when the earlier one already decided. Use `thenBy` when that matters.

entries.name: reverse
entries.summary: Swaps Less and Greater and fixes Equal — descending order.

entries.name: thenBy
entries.summary:
Short-circuiting `combine`: the tie-breaker block runs only when this comparison is Equal, so it costs nothing once the order is decided.

```kex
a.name.compare(b.name).thenBy { a.age.compare(b.age) }
```

entries.name: Bits
entries.summary:
The `Bits` module provides bitwise operations on `Integer`.

Integers are arbitrary precision, and a negative one behaves as if it were written in infinite-precision two's complement — so `Bits.not(0)` is `-1` and `Bits.and(-1, 255)` is `255`, with no word size to overflow. Shifts and bit indices count from bit 0 (the least significant bit).

entries.name: and
entries.summary: Bitwise AND of `a` and `b`.

entries.name: or
entries.summary: Bitwise OR of `a` and `b`.

entries.name: xor
entries.summary: Bitwise exclusive OR of `a` and `b`.

entries.name: not
entries.summary: Bitwise complement of `a`. Every integer is signed and unbounded, so this is always +-(a + 1)+ rather than a width-dependent mask.

entries.name: shiftLeft
entries.summary: Shifts `n` left by `by` bits. Raises if `by` is negative.

entries.name: shiftRight
entries.summary: Shifts `n` right by `by` bits, propagating the sign — the result of shifting a negative number stays negative. Raises if `by` is negative.

entries.name: test?
entries.summary: True when the bit at `index` of `n` is set. Raises if `index` is negative.

entries.name: set
entries.summary: `n` with the bit at `index` set. Raises if `index` is negative.

entries.name: clear
entries.summary: `n` with the bit at `index` cleared. Raises if `index` is negative.

entries.name: toggle
entries.summary: `n` with the bit at `index` flipped. Raises if `index` is negative.

entries.name: count
entries.summary: Number of set bits in `n` (population count). A negative value has infinitely many under two's complement, so this raises for one.

entries.name: width
entries.summary: Number of bits needed to represent `n`, i.e. the position of its highest set bit plus one. Zero needs none. Raises for a negative value.

entries.name: Console
entries.summary: ANSI terminal styling. Color constants become empty strings when Kex is started with --no-colors, so callers can compose them without branching.

entries.name: colorize
entries.summary: Wrap `text` in an ANSI style and reset attributes afterwards.

entries.name: enabled?
entries.summary: Whether terminal styling is enabled for this process.

entries.name: Digest
entries.summary: Cryptographic content digests. Hex strings are used at the public boundary so Kex programs never need to handle backend-specific binary values.

entries.name: Errorable
entries.summary: Errorable — the trait for values that describe a failure. Implemented by error types that carry a human-readable message, so generic handlers can display or log any error uniformly (independent of the concrete error type's structured fields).

entries.name: ParseError
entries.summary: ParseError — a typed parse failure. Carries the original `input`, the byte `position` where parsing stopped (and from which it can be continued), the successfully parsed `value` (if any prefix was consumed — typed `Any` so it works across Integer / Float / Number), a diagnostic `message`, and the remaining unconsumed suffix `rest` so the caller can resume parsing.

entries.name: Evaluator
signatures: run(source: String, opts: EvaluatorOptions) -> Result<Any, String>
runExpression(source: String, opts: EvaluatorOptions) -> Result<Any, String>
entries.summary:
Sandboxed evaluation of Kex source code at runtime.

Creates a fresh, isolated evaluator for each call — the caller's environment is never shared. Returns `Result<Any, String>`.

entries.name: run
signatures: run(source: String, opts: EvaluatorOptions) -> Result<Any, String>
entries.summary: Evaluates a full Kex program string.

entries.name: runExpression
signatures: runExpression(source: String, opts: EvaluatorOptions) -> Result<Any, String>
entries.summary: Evaluates a single Kex expression.

entries.name: getLine
entries.summary: Compatibility names matching IO-style handle operations.

entries.name: sum
entries.summary: Sums all elements. Returns `0` for an empty list.

entries.name: product
entries.summary: Multiplies all elements. Returns `1` for an empty list.

entries.name: product
entries.summary: Maps each element through `f` and multiplies the results.

entries.name: min
entries.summary: Returns the smallest element wrapped in `Just`, or `None` for an empty list.

entries.name: max
entries.summary: Returns the largest element wrapped in `Just`, or `None` for an empty list.

entries.name: [X]
signatures: reduce(acc: A, f: (A -> X -> A)) -> A

entries.name: first
entries.summary: Returns the first element wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if the list is empty.

entries.name: second
entries.summary: Returns the second element wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if the list has fewer than two elements.

entries.name: third
entries.summary: Returns the third element wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if the list has fewer than three elements.

entries.name: rest
entries.summary: Returns all elements after the first. Returns `[]` for an empty or single-element list.

entries.name: last
entries.summary: Returns the last element wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if the list is empty.

entries.name: count
entries.summary: Returns the number of elements. When given a predicate, returns the count of elements for which it holds.

entries.name: length
entries.summary: Compatibility spelling shared with String.

entries.name: count
entries.summary: count(pred) is provided by the Enumerable trait.

entries.name: empty?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the list contains no elements.

entries.name: find
entries.summary:
Returns the first element satisfying the predicate wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if no element matches.

find/any?/all? are provided by the Enumerable trait.

entries.name: any?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if at least one element satisfies the predicate.

entries.name: all?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if every element satisfies the predicate.

entries.name: map
entries.summary:
Transforms each element by applying `f`.

map/filter/each are provided by the Enumerable trait (in terms of reduce).

entries.name: filter
entries.summary: Returns a new list containing only the elements for which `pred` is `true`.

entries.name: reject
entries.summary: Returns a new list with all elements for which `pred` is `true` removed. The inverse of `filter`.

entries.name: each
entries.summary: Calls `f` with each element for its side effects. Returns unit.

entries.name: reduce
signatures: reduce(acc: A, f: (A -> X -> A)) -> A
entries.summary: Folds the list from the left, starting with `acc` and combining each element via `f`.

entries.name: flatMap
entries.summary: Maps each element to a list and concatenates the results.

entries.name: at
entries.summary: Returns the element at position `i` (0-based) wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if the index is out of range.

entries.name: contains?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if `elem` is present in the list.

entries.name: indexOf
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the first index at which `elem` appears, wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if the element is not present.

entries.name: findIndex
entries.summary: Returns the index of the first element satisfying `pred`, wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if none does. The predicate counterpart of `indexOf`, which searches by value.

entries.name: takeWhile
entries.summary: Returns the longest leading run of elements satisfying `pred`. Stops at the first element that does not, so it is not `filter` — later matches are dropped with everything after the first failure.

entries.name: dropWhile
entries.summary: Returns what is left after `takeWhile` — everything from the first element that does not satisfy `pred` onwards.

entries.name: uniq
entries.summary: Returns a new list with duplicate elements removed, preserving the first occurrence of each element.

entries.name: partition
entries.summary: Splits the list into two lists: those for which `pred` is `true` (first) and those for which it is `false` (second).

entries.name: collect
entries.summary: Maps each element through `f` (which returns an `Optional`), keeping and unwrapping the `Just(y)` results and dropping `None`. Filter + map fused.

entries.name: take
entries.summary: Returns the first `n` elements.

entries.name: drop
entries.summary: Drops the first `n` elements.

entries.name: push
entries.summary: Returns a new list with `x` appended at the end.

entries.name: reverse
entries.summary: Returns the elements in reverse order.

entries.name: zip
entries.summary: Pairs each element of this list with the corresponding element of `other`. Stops at the end of the shorter list.

entries.name: flatten
entries.summary: Flattens exactly one level of nesting. Only valid on lists of lists.

entries.name: sort
entries.summary: Returns the elements sorted in ascending natural order.

entries.name: sort
entries.summary: Returns the elements sorted using a custom comparator. `comp` should return `true` when its first argument should come before its second.

entries.name: min
entries.summary: Returns the element with the smallest `f` key wrapped in `Just`, or `None` for an empty list.

entries.name: max
entries.summary: Returns the element with the largest `f` key wrapped in `Just`, or `None` for an empty list.

entries.name: sum
entries.summary: Maps each element through `f` and sums the results.

entries.name: join
entries.summary: Receiver is `[X]`, not `[String | Char]`: the intrinsic renders whatever it is given, so `[1, 2].join(", ")` is "1, 2" on both backends. The narrower receiver only ever fired once element types became precise enough to catch it — until then `map`/`filter` handed `join` an unknown element type and the restriction checked nothing. Concatenates all elements, placing `sep` between each adjacent pair. With no separator the elements are joined directly.

entries.name: Map
entries.summary: Declared for the same reason list.kex declares `type List<X> = [X]`: it gives the name `Map` a source declaration, so it resolves as a type through the collected interfaces rather than needing to be known to the compiler.

entries.name: Map<K, V>
signatures: put(k: K, v: V) -> Map<K, V>

entries.name: reduce
entries.summary: Enumerable primitive: fold over (key, value) pairs in canonical (sorted) order. Collection-producing operations come from Enumerable and traversal queries come from Foldable; their two-arg blocks auto-splat each pair.

entries.name: identity
entries.summary: Maps form a right-biased Monoid under merge.

entries.name: get
entries.summary: Returns the value for `key` wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if absent. When a `default` is supplied, returns the raw unwrapped value instead.

entries.name: put
signatures: put(k: K, v: V) -> Map<K, V>
entries.summary: Returns a new map with `key` mapped to `value`. Use `put!` to rebind the receiver variable.

entries.name: delete
entries.summary: Returns a new map without `key`. No-op if the key is absent. Use `delete!` to rebind the receiver variable.

entries.name: has?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if `key` exists in the map.

entries.name: empty?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the map has no entries.

entries.name: count
entries.summary: Returns the number of key-value pairs. When given a predicate, counts only matching entries.

entries.name: keys
entries.summary: Returns all keys as a list, in insertion order.

entries.name: values
entries.summary: Returns all values as a list, in insertion order.

entries.name: entries
entries.summary: Returns all key-value pairs as a list of tuples, in insertion order.

entries.name: each
entries.summary: Calls `f` with each key-value pair for its side effects.

entries.name: map
entries.summary: Transforms each entry by calling `f(k, v)`. Returns a list of results.

entries.name: mapValues
entries.summary: Returns a new map with all values transformed by `f`.

entries.name: mapKeys
entries.summary: Returns a new map with all keys transformed by `f`.

entries.name: filter
entries.summary:
Returns a new map keeping only entries for which `pred` returns `true`.

Map overrides the map-returning HOFs (Enumerable's default returns a list).

entries.name: reject
entries.summary: Returns a new map with all entries for which `pred` returns `true` removed.

entries.name: merge
entries.summary: Returns a new map combining `this` and `other`. On key conflict, `other`'s value wins.

entries.name: any?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if at least one entry satisfies `pred`.

entries.name: all?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if every entry satisfies `pred`.

entries.name: find
entries.summary: Returns the first entry satisfying `pred` as a tuple wrapped in `Just`, or `None` if no entry matches.

entries.name: Math
entries.summary: The `Math` module provides standard mathematical constants and functions. All trigonometric functions operate in radians. A Kex `Float` is always finite, so a domain error (`Math.sqrt(-1.0)`) or an overflow (`Math.exp(1000.0)`) raises rather than producing `NaN` or `Infinity` — the same rule BEAM enforces, where those two values cannot exist at all.

entries.name: PI
entries.summary: Math.PI : Float Ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

entries.name: E
entries.summary: Math.E : Float Base of the natural logarithm.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.summary: Square root of `x`. Raises for negative input, which has no real root.

entries.name: cbrt
entries.summary: Cube root of `x`.

entries.name: sin
entries.summary: Sine of `x` (radians).

entries.name: cos
entries.summary: Cosine of `x` (radians).

entries.name: tan
entries.summary: Tangent of `x` (radians).

entries.name: asin
entries.summary: Inverse sine (arc sine) of `x`, result in radians.

entries.name: acos
entries.summary: Inverse cosine (arc cosine) of `x`, result in radians.

entries.name: atan
entries.summary: Inverse tangent (arc tangent) of `x`, result in radians in (-π/2, π/2).

entries.name: atan2
entries.summary: Two-argument arc tangent. Returns the angle of vector (`x`, `y`) in (-π, π]. Handles the sign of both arguments to place the result in the correct quadrant.

entries.name: sinh
entries.summary: Hyperbolic sine.

entries.name: cosh
entries.summary: Hyperbolic cosine.

entries.name: tanh
entries.summary: Hyperbolic tangent.

entries.name: log
entries.summary: Natural logarithm of `x` (base e). With two arguments, computes log base `base`.

entries.name: log2
entries.summary: Base-2 logarithm of `x`.

entries.name: log10
entries.summary: Base-10 logarithm of `x`.

entries.name: exp
entries.summary: `e` raised to the power `x`.

entries.name: pow
entries.summary: `x` raised to the power `y`.

entries.name: abs
entries.summary: Absolute value of `x`.

entries.name: floor
entries.summary: Floor of `x` — largest integer not greater than `x`.

entries.name: ceil
entries.summary: Ceiling of `x` — smallest integer not less than `x`.

entries.name: hypot
entries.summary: Euclidean distance — equivalent to +sqrt(x*x + y*y)+ but avoids intermediate overflow for large values.

entries.name: even?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the integer is even.

entries.name: odd?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the integer is odd.

entries.name: abs
entries.summary: Returns the absolute value.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.summary: Returns the square root as a Float.

entries.name: modulo
entries.summary: Returns `this` modulo `n`. The result has the same sign as `n`, consistent with mathematical modulo (not C remainder).

entries.name: in?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the integer falls within `range` (inclusive).

entries.name: times
entries.summary: Calls `f` exactly `this` times, passing the current index (0-based).

entries.name: floor
entries.summary: Returns the greatest integer ≤ this. No-op on integers.

entries.name: ceil
entries.summary: Returns the smallest integer ≥ this. No-op on integers.

entries.name: round
entries.summary: Rounds to the nearest integer. No-op on integers.

entries.name: abs
entries.summary: Returns the absolute value.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.summary: Returns the square root.

entries.name: in?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the float falls within `range` (inclusive).

entries.name: floor
entries.summary: Returns the greatest integer ≤ this.

entries.name: ceil
entries.summary: Returns the smallest integer ≥ this.

entries.name: round
entries.summary: Rounds to the nearest integer.

entries.name: toInteger
entries.summary: Truncates toward zero, converting to an `Integer`.

entries.name: Integer
signatures: parse(s: String, radix: Integer) -> Result<Integer, ParseError>

entries.name: parse
signatures: parse(s: String, radix: Integer) -> Result<Integer, ParseError>
entries.summary: Parses `s` in base `radix` (2..36), e.g. `Integer.parse("ff", radix: 16)`. Digits above 9 are accepted in either case.

entries.name: Optional
entries.summary: `X?` is shorthand for `Optional<X>`. `Just(x)` wraps a value; `None` represents absence.

entries.name: Result
entries.summary: `Result<X, E>` represents a computation that either succeeded with `Ok(x)` or failed with `Error(e)`.

entries.name: Either
entries.summary: `Either<L, R>` holds one of two possible value types.

entries.name: Optionable
entries.summary: Marker traits used by generic code that accepts one of these ADT families. Their conformances are exported through KexI like any user-defined trait.

entries.name: set?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if this optional has value.

entries.name: none?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if this optional is empty.

entries.name: or
entries.summary: Unwraps the value, returning `default` when `None`.

entries.name: map
entries.summary: Applies `f` to the wrapped value, leaving `None` unchanged.

entries.name: flatMap
entries.summary: Chains optional-returning functions, short-circuiting on `None`.

entries.name: ok?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the result is `Ok`.

entries.name: error?
entries.summary: Returns `true` if the result is `Error`.

entries.name: or
entries.summary: Unwraps the `Ok` value, returning `default` on `Error`.

entries.name: map
entries.summary: Applies `f` to the `Ok` value, passing `Error` through unchanged.

entries.name: flatMap
entries.summary: Chains result-returning functions, propagating `Error`.

entries.name: optional
entries.summary: Converts to `Optional`, discarding the error value on failure.

entries.name: or
entries.summary: Universal `.or(default)` catch-all: a value that is neither Optional nor Result is already a successful result — return it unchanged.

entries.name: to
entries.summary:
Universal `.to(Type)` conversion. The type argument is a runtime Type value (e.g. String, Integer, Float, List). Returns an Optional result.

Optional, NOT Result, and deliberately: `to` is the everyday conversion, and what it can report on failure is almost always derivable from the types alone — `x.to(List)` on a non-list fails because a non-list is not a list, which an error payload saying "cannot convert Int to List" does not improve. When the reason IS information — where a parse gave up and on what — `Integer.parse`/`Float.parse` answer with `Result<_, ParseError>`. So: `to` for every day, `parse` when the failure needs handling.

A String target goes through the Showable protocol, exactly as `make Showable do let to(String) = Just(this.showValue)` says it does. The intrinsic below renders the raw runtime term instead, which on BEAM never reached the `Optional` implementation of showValue: `Just(42).to(String)` answered `Just("Just(42)")` there and `Just("42")` on the tree walker, which dispatches to the Showable clause. Intrinsics cannot call back into the prelude (dependency_layering_test), so the protocol has to be honoured here.

entries.name: Parser
entries.summary:
Parses Kex source code into a structured AST at runtime.

Returns `Result<Program, ParseError>` — the AST includes module definitions, function signatures, type/record definitions, traits, make blocks, and doc-comments extracted from `#` lines.

Function bodies are intentionally omitted from the output.

entries.name: parse
entries.summary: Parses a Kex source string into a structured AST.

entries.name: parseFile
entries.summary: Reads a file and parses it.

entries.name: parseType
entries.summary: Parses a type expression string into a TypeRef.

entries.name: parseExpression
entries.summary: Parses a single expression string into an Expression AST node.

entries.name: TypeRef
entries.summary: Structured representation of type expressions.

entries.name: toString
entries.summary: Pretty-prints the type reference to a human-readable string.

entries.name: PatternRef
entries.summary: Structured representation of patterns.

entries.name: toString
entries.summary: Pretty-prints the pattern to a human-readable string.

entries.name: Expression
entries.summary: Structured representation of expression AST nodes.

entries.name: Range
entries.summary: Range — a range computes everything from its two bounds; `items` materializes the elements into a real list when one is needed.

entries.name: reduce
entries.summary: Shared primitive for Enumerable and Foldable. Range stays structurally minimal; inherited operations reduce over its materialized items in ascending range order.

entries.name: sum
entries.summary: Numeric range aggregates are expressed in terms of the Enumerable primitive rather than relying on the walker's historical List fallback.

entries.name: contains?
entries.summary: Membership is a Range method, not a fallback into the bare String/List native dispatcher.

entries.name: items
entries.summary: The range's elements as a list.

entries.name: first
entries.summary: The list operations, over the materialized items. A range is an ordered collection, so `(1..5).first` and `(1..5).length` are questions it can answer — and on the BEAM backend, where a range IS its item list, they already worked. Only the walker rejected them ("Undefined method: first for Range"), so every one of these was a backend divergence rather than a deliberate restriction.

entries.name: Sequence
entries.summary: Creates an infinite stream starting at `from`, applying `step` to produce each successive element.

entries.name: Iterate
entries.summary: Creates an infinite stream seeded with `seed`, applying `f` to each element to produce the next. Equivalent to `Sequence`; use whichever reads more clearly at the call site.

entries.name: take
entries.summary: Returns the first `n` elements as a list. Evaluates the stream up to that point.

entries.name: drop
entries.summary: Skips the first `n` elements and returns a new stream offset by `n`.

entries.name: map
entries.summary: Returns a new stream applying `f` to each element.

entries.name: filter
entries.summary: Returns a new stream keeping only elements for which `pred` is `true`. Note: consuming `n` elements may require evaluating many upstream elements.

entries.name: TaggedValidation
entries.summary: Diagnostics returned by optional compile-time tagged-literal validators. Byte offsets are zero-based and relative to the cooked literal body.

entries.name: describe
entries.summary: Groups related test cases under a label. Calls the block immediately. `describe` blocks may be nested. This is a foul function — it prints output.

entries.name: it
entries.summary: Defines a single test case. The block is run and any exception thrown inside it (typically a failed `assert`) marks the test failed without aborting the rest of the suite. This is a foul function — it prints output.

entries.name: before
entries.summary: Registers setup for the current group. `before { ... }` and `before(:each) { ... }` run before every test; `before(:all) { ... }` runs once before the group's tests, following RSpec's scope convention.

entries.name: after
entries.summary: Registers cleanup for the current group. `after { ... }` defaults to `:each`; `after(:all) { ... }` runs once when the group finishes. Cleanup is unconditional, and inner per-test hooks run before outer hooks.

entries.name: assert
entries.summary: Throws a runtime error if `value` is falsy, failing the enclosing `it`. The optional `message` is included in the failure output.

entries.name: Assert
entries.summary: Focused assertions are ordinary Kex stdlib functions layered on the primitive `assert`, so adding another helper does not require compiler or runtime work.
